The exact guard_fact for the two candidate carrier transitions (transition:line:22 with guard R45RouteToken==6, transition:line:23 with guard R45RouteToken==7) shows only opaque integer-token equality guards; the brake-pressed condition is folded into the internally-fired trigger names at lines 15 and 16 rather than expressed as an evaluable guard predicate, and the AutoFinalState-sourced edge (line 16/23) carries no explicit auto-final-membership or brake-pressed guard of its own. This is a precise, source-grounded mismatch between the NL's declared exact condition and the parsed guard expression. The strongest alternative reading -- that the route-token macro is a faithful lowering satisfying the compound obligation through its whole member set -- is a rebutting defeater in kind, but this correction's defeater_evidence_reference_catalog for this obligation is empty, so no exact catalog token can be cited to support that the macro's source endpoints, member digest, and target-entry segment actually close under a macro-satisfaction rule. Because a surviving typed defeater requires at least one exact catalog reference and none exists here, the rebuttal cannot be marked as surviving; it is defeated, and the exact guard_fact establishes the violation.

result.reason: This lens focuses on behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and stable termination. Key finding: NL5-TERMINATION-1 requires the system to reach a stable Final completion on power off. Inspection shows all Power_Off consumer transitions (from HumanDrivingMode, AutoInitialState, AutoOperationalState, AutoFinalState) resolve to [*] either directly (HumanDrivingMode line:27) or via the R45RouteToken==9 synthetic routing (AutonomousMode line:24), both closing to root [*]/Final. This is syntactically stable and closed, so NL5-TERMINATION-1 and NL5-ENDPOINT-1 are satisfied and omitted. Event consumer coverage for all five events shows reachable consumers matching declared consumers exactly (verified from inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers), so no coverage gap exists for any event, including Power_Off. Root reachability: all six states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection facts, so no reachability defect exists for AutonomousMode substates or HumanDrivingMode; NL2-ELEMENT-1, NL2-DERIVED containment, and NL4.2-DERIVED containment (auto final contained in AutonomousMode) are satisfied and omitted. The critical remaining behavioral-consequence issue is on NL4.2's guard obligation: the NL requires a composite trigger 'receive human steering cmd' plus a conjunctive guard 'brake pressed AND in (auto final)' on the AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode relation. The closed model's actual carrier transitions (AutoOperationalState->[*] at line 15, AutoFinalState->[*] at line 16) that consume the merged trigger human_steering_cmd_brake_pressed both have guard=null; and the outer AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transitions (line 22, 23) only carry a synthetic R45RouteToken equality guard, which is a compiler-generated routing artifact rather than the authored 'brake pressed'/'in (auto final)' predicate. No exact carrier transition anywhere expresses the required conjunctive guard as an independently evaluated boolean condition. This confirms NL4.2-GUARD-1 (aliased REF-008) as a behavior-consequence candidate: the required guard content is functionally absent even though the trigger and endpoint exist. I retain the source/target concept identity via element_refs on the candidate rather than via semantic_bindings, since the exact refs are directly nameable FCSTM state/transition refs and do not require a separate ambiguous binding. No additional_contracts are needed since this gap is already captured by the supplied NL4.2-GUARD-1 contract's exact locus/property/direction.

issues.expected: The AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode transition must carry a guard/trigger conjunction equivalent to 'brake pressed AND currently in AutoFinalState' (the NL's 'in (auto final)' sub-state check), tied to the same transition that receives the human steering command event.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM realizes the return relation as two separate root-level transitions (transition:line:22 guard R45RouteToken==6, transition:line:23 guard R45RouteToken==7) triggered internally by human_steering_cmd_brake_pressed events fired inside AutoOperationalState (line 15, unguarded) and AutoFinalState (line 16, unguarded) respectively, and the AutoFinalState-sourced edge (line 16/23) has no explicit brake-pressed or auto-final state-check guard of its own -- the sub-state membership is encoded only implicitly by which internal state fired the event, not as an evaluable guard expression. The 'brake pressed' condition is folded into the trigger name rather than expressed as an independent guard, and no exact guard predicate equivalent to the compound condition is present on either carrier transition.
issues.reason: NL4.2-GUARD-1 requires an exact conjunctive guard (brake pressed AND in auto final) on the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition. The closed model's exact guard_fact shows only opaque integer-token equality guards (R45RouteToken==6/==7) on the two root-level candidate carriers, with no explicit brake-pressed or auto-final-membership predicate value in the parsed guard field. branches.reason: This lens focuses on behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and stable termination. Key finding: NL5-TERMINATION-1 requires the system to reach a stable Final completion on power off. Inspection shows all Power_Off consumer transitions (from HumanDrivingMode, AutoInitialState, AutoOperationalState, AutoFinalState) resolve to [*] either directly (HumanDrivingMode line:27) or via the R45RouteToken==9 synthetic routing (AutonomousMode line:24), both closing to root [*]/Final. This is syntactically stable and closed, so NL5-TERMINATION-1 and NL5-ENDPOINT-1 are satisfied and omitted. Event consumer coverage for all five events shows reachable consumers matching declared consumers exactly (verified from inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers), so no coverage gap exists for any event, including Power_Off. Root reachability: all six states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection facts, so no reachability defect exists for AutonomousMode substates or HumanDrivingMode; NL2-ELEMENT-1, NL2-DERIVED containment, and NL4.2-DERIVED containment (auto final contained in AutonomousMode) are satisfied and omitted. The critical remaining behavioral-consequence issue is on NL4.2's guard obligation: the NL requires a composite trigger 'receive human steering cmd' plus a conjunctive guard 'brake pressed AND in (auto final)' on the AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode relation. The closed model's actual carrier transitions (AutoOperationalState->[*] at line 15, AutoFinalState->[*] at line 16) that consume the merged trigger human_steering_cmd_brake_pressed both have guard=null; and the outer AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transitions (line 22, 23) only carry a synthetic R45RouteToken equality guard, which is a compiler-generated routing artifact rather than the authored 'brake pressed'/'in (auto final)' predicate. No exact carrier transition anywhere expresses the required conjunctive guard as an independently evaluated boolean condition. This confirms NL4.2-GUARD-1 (aliased REF-008) as a behavior-consequence candidate: the required guard content is functionally absent even though the trigger and endpoint exist. I retain the source/target concept identity via element_refs on the candidate rather than via semantic_bindings, since the exact refs are directly nameable FCSTM state/transition refs and do not require a separate ambiguous binding. No additional_contracts are needed since this gap is already captured by the supplied NL4.2-GUARD-1 contract's exact locus/property/direction.
